dims_mm.note: ASUS: 28.0 x 11.1 x 2.12 ~ 3.24 cm (W x D x H). d is the thinnest point, d_max the grips.

weight_g.note: NotebookCheck spec table: 611 g, power supply 223 g. The Ally X review repeats 611 g for the original Ally.

slots.note: M.2 2230 NVMe, user-replaceable behind the back cover

ports.note: Combo port with the XG Mobile interface. DisplayPort 1.4. pd_in_w is the bundled 65 W USB-C adapter rating.
ROG XG Mobile eGPU interface; shares one combo housing with the USB-C port
UHS-II; supports SD, SDXC and SDHC

screen.note: IPS-level, anti-glare low-reflection, 100% sRGB, 7 ms, AMD FreeSync Premium, Gorilla Glass Victus + DXC

battery.note: 40 Wh 4S1P 4-cell Li-ion. 65 W USB-C adapter (inclusion varies by region).

controls.stick_note: 2 x full-size analog sticks. NotebookCheck: the sticks have no Hall sensors.
controls.note: ASUS: L & R Hall Effect analog triggers, 2 x assignable grip buttons, 6-axis IMU

notes: One ASUS spec page (RC71L) covers the Z1 and Z1 Extreme rows. Black and white colorways share this hardware. ASUS lists Bluetooth 5.4 and says the version may change with the OS version.

unresolved.reason: ASUS gives no speed, DP or PD data for the XG Mobile interface itself; video and power run through the USB-C side of the combo port
speed_gbps, dp_alt and pd_in_w do not apply to the 3.5mm jack
dp_alt and pd_in_w do not apply to a card reader; the vendor gives the bus standard (see note), not a Gbps figure
ASUS and NotebookCheck give PCIe 4.0 but not the lane count
ASUS gives one brightness value (500 nits); no HDR or peak figure
Sources say only that the sticks are not Hall effect; no source names the sensor
Not stated by ASUS or the reviews used

'The triggers at the top use hall sensors, so there are no hall sensors for the sticks'
